name: William Hornbuckle
current_role: CEO & President, MGM Resorts International; director, GBank Financial Holdings
profile: Bill Hornbuckle is a Las Vegas hospitality veteran who joined MGM in 1998, rose through COO and CMO roles, and became MGM Resorts CEO in 2020. His contract runs through 2028, after which he is slated to advise on MGM's ~$9B Osaka integrated resort. He also co-chairs MGM China and chairs the U.S. Travel Association.
interesting_fact: He helped bring the Raiders and the WNBA Aces to Las Vegas and served as president of T-Mobile Arena; he co-founded GBank (formerly Bank of George).
deep_cut_fact: Born on a U.S. Air Force base in Japan and raised in Connecticut, he found hospitality bartending at 18, drove cross-country to UNLV's hotel school, and started as a room-service attendant and busboy at the Jockey Club; he was on the opening team of The Mirage.
notes: Japan (Osaka) angle and energy/infrastructure of mega-resorts could be a podcast hook. Route via MGM corporate communications.

name: Denise C Johnson
current_role: Group President, Resource Industries, Caterpillar Inc. (retiring Feb 1, 2027; advisory role during transition)
profile: Denise Johnson is a Michigan State mechanical engineer and MIT LGO alumna who spent two decades at GM (product development, labor relations VP, head of GM Brazil) before joining Caterpillar in 2011. She has led Caterpillar's mining equipment group, Resource Industries, since 2016, returning it to profitability and making Cat a leader in mining autonomy. Caterpillar announced in Oct 2026 that she will retire Feb 1, 2027.
interesting_fact: She was the first woman in Caterpillar's history to lead one of its business groups, and oversaw the scale-up of Cat's autonomous mining truck fleet.
deep_cut_fact: Facing her first union negotiation as GM's labor-relations VP after the 2009 bankruptcy, she pulled out her old MIT LGO negotiations-class notes, including her written list of BATNAs.
notes: Retiring Feb 2027 (successor Derrick York from Nov 1, 2026) per Caterpillar release https://www.caterpillar.com/en/news/corporate-press-releases/h/caterpillar-announces-leadership-transition-in-resource-industries.html. Mining electrification/autonomy is a strong energy-podcast angle; post-retirement she may be more available. Route via Caterpillar corporate communications.

name: Giang Nguyen
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Opendoor Technologies (since ~Nov 2025); publicly known as Giang LeGrice
profile: Giang (Nguyen) LeGrice is Opendoor's COO, leading market operations, efficiency and customer experience. She spent roughly 2019-2025 at Shopify, rising to VP of Operations, where she ran ops transformation, FP&A and business analytics. New Opendoor CEO Kaz Nejatian, her former boss at Shopify, recruited her in late 2025 as part of his AI-led overhaul.
interesting_fact: Kaz Nejatian called her his 'second-in-command' at Shopify and a 'world-class leader', saying he trusts no one more to help Opendoor 'find the next gear'.
notes: SEC Form 4 filer name is 'Giang Nguyen' (CIK 2096999) while Opendoor's own pages use 'Giang LeGrice'; same COO role, almost certainly the same person under legal vs. public name. Low public profile; route via Opendoor investor relations/press (investor.opendoor.com).

name: William L Ballhaus
current_role: Chairman & CEO (and President), Mercury Systems; employment extended Sept 2026
profile: Bill Ballhaus is a serial aerospace/defense and tech CEO: he ran DynCorp International (2008-10) and SRA International, then was Chairman & CEO of Blackboard (2016-21) before taking over Mercury Systems, the defense electronics maker. Earlier he held senior roles at BAE Systems, Boeing and Hughes. He is also Executive Chairman of Catalis and a director of Everfox.
interesting_fact: He has led companies across very different sectors: defense contracting (DynCorp), government IT, and edtech (Blackboard, through its merger with Anthology) before Mercury.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trained aerospace engineer: a UC Davis mechanical engineering BS plus master's and doctorate in Aeronautics and Astronautics from Stanford, and an MBA from UCLA Anderson.
notes: Mercury corporate communications (Sr. Director Turner Brinton) handles press per newsroom. Web search budget ran out during this lane; facts here are from Mercury's own site.

name: Andrew D Ross
current_role: President & Chief Operating Officer, Parker-Hannifin; director, Symbotic Inc.
profile: Andy Ross is a long-time Parker-Hannifin operating executive who ran the Engineered Materials Group (2012-15) and Fluid Connectors Group (2015-22), became COO in Jan 2023 and President in Jan 2024 under CEO Jennifer Parmentier. He is a named executive officer of the Cleveland motion-and-control giant and sits on the board of warehouse-robotics company Symbotic.
interesting_fact: He was elevated to COO in the same 2022 succession that made Jennifer Parmentier Parker's CEO, and added the President title when Thomas Banks retired at the start of 2024.

name: Mark Adam Wallace
current_role: Retired (former SVP & Chief Customer Officer, Keysight Technologies; announced retirement effective by end of May 2025)
profile: Mark Wallace is a career test-and-measurement sales executive who held sales, marketing and channel leadership roles at Hewlett-Packard, Agilent and Keysight. He ran Keysight's Americas field operations, then led worldwide sales from Nov 2016 and served as SVP & Chief Customer Officer from Sept 2022 until retiring in 2025.
interesting_fact: His career spans the full HP lineage: Hewlett-Packard, its 1999 spin-off Agilent, and Agilent's 2014 spin-off Keysight, where he became head of global sales.
notes: Retired per Keysight 8-K of Nov 4, 2024 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1601046/000160104624000065/keys-20241104.htm). Very low public profile; no published personal contact found. Web search budget ran out during this lane.

name: Phong Le
current_role: President & CEO, Strategy Inc (formerly MicroStrategy), since Aug 2022
profile: Phong Le joined MicroStrategy as CFO in 2015 after finance roles at XO Communications, NII Holdings and 12 years at Deloitte consulting; he added COO in 2018 and became CEO in 2022 when Michael Saylor moved to executive chairman. He now runs the company's bitcoin-treasury and 'Digital Credit' strategy; Strategy held ~848,500 BTC as of Oct 2026.
interesting_fact: In Q3 2026 Strategy reported $21B of operating income, its largest ever, and said it had raised $21B of equity year-to-date while growing bitcoin holdings 26%.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance, he trained as an engineer: he holds a B.S. in Biomedical Engineering from Johns Hopkins (plus an MIT Sloan MBA), and spent 1998-2010 in Deloitte's consulting practice.
notes: Bitcoin mining/energy angle is a natural podcast hook. Active on X and podcasts, but handle not verified here (web search budget ran out); check before citing. Strategy website blocks automated access.
